subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should webhook deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, queued, serialized, or left parallel by default, and should that behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The requested 409 changes an external HTTP webhook contract and retry semantics for existing integrations, while related persistent-session and queued-webhook work could choose a different same-session overlap policy.

options.title: Opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip, queue, or parallel while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

options.title: Unconditional 409 guard
options.body: Implement the reporter's exact fail-fast behavior for every same-session active hook delivery and accept the compatibility change.

options.title: Fold into webhook queues
options.body: Defer this guard until queued webhook support decides durable backlog, parallelism, and caller response semantics together.

recommendation.title: Opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip, queue, or parallel while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting external API compatibility choice and steipete is the strongest available routing owner from prior hook/cron history and fallback ownership.
